title: An entropic bottleneck, dynamical gating, and outward redistribution of roaming in a designed Chesnavich-type model
summary: Roaming reactions are organized not by potential-energy saddles but by transition states that are unstable invariant objects in phase space, periodic orbits in the two degrees of freedom studied here. To ask what controls roaming, we modify the Chesnavich model of a barrierless ion--molecule dissociation: its orientation-dependent angular hindrance is replaced by a transverse-stiffness ridge whose angular frequency peaks at an interior radius, and the classical dynamics are studied at a fixed energy just above the dissociation threshold.
